text: Jonah felt sick and stayed home from school. A parcel was waiting for him at the post office, and he wondered if it was still open. He picked up his phone and typed two words: "Post office?" The assistant told him it closed at five o'clock and was a ten minute walk from his flat. Jonah wrote, "Remind me." The assistant set a reminder for four o'clock that said, pick up the parcel. Then Jonah asked, "How much is the fee?" The assistant said the fee was three euro and that the clerk took coins. Jonah smiled, put a few coins in his pocket, and rested on the sofa until the reminder buzzed.

A booking is a promise to be somewhere at a set time. People make bookings for haircuts, the dentist and the doctor. The shop keeps a list of times, and each time holds only one person. Opening hours tell you when you can come. Sometimes plans change, so people say, "Move my haircut to Friday," or "Cancel my dentist visit." It is true that many clinics close early on Saturday, so ask first. Most waiting rooms have an air purifier, and the chairs are comfortable. If you drive, ask where you can park near the door. If you will be late, say, "I will be ten minutes late," so they can plan.

Aiko was driving home when she remembered the kitchen speaker. Her kids had left it playing a funny song at full volume. She said to her phone, "Turn the kitchen speaker down, but don't stop the music." The assistant lowered the volume to a soft level and kept the song going. Aiko laughed and said, "Search for another funny song, but not the one about the frog." The assistant searched and added a silly song about a cat to the queue. It also said, "The dryer finished a minute ago." "Tell me later, I don't want to hear about it now," said Aiko. The assistant said it would wait, and Aiko turned onto her street smiling.

The news tells you what is happening in the world, in your town, or in sport. A headline is a short line that sums up a story. People change the topic, the place and how many stories they hear. They say, "Read me the local headlines," "Give me sports scores only," or "Skip the weather." On a slow morning you might chill with a cup of tea and hear that a food truck in the park is selling delicious soup. If you want less, say, "Just three stories." If you want more, say, "Tell me more about that one." The news keeps changing, so ask again later for fresh updates.

Person: Can you book a room for my family?
Assistant: Yes. Which city is the hotel in?
Person: Lisbon. We want to arrive early on Thursday.
Assistant: How many nights will you stay?
Person: Three nights. Does the hotel have a good network for my tablet?
Assistant: Most hotels have free wifi. I will check this one. Is there anything else you need?
Person: Can the hotel heat our room before we come?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't do that. I can send the staff a note asking them.
Person: Yes, please. Mum says the breakfast there is healthy.
Assistant: Great. I will book three nights and send the note.

Oscar came home after a night shift, tired but happy. He wanted to make a paper model for his niece's birthday. He said to his phone, "Find a good tutorial for a paper boat." The assistant found one. Then Oscar said, "Wait, I mean a paper plane, not a boat." The assistant changed the search and showed three plane tutorials. He asked it to reduce the video speed to half so he could follow along, and the assistant slowed the video. Then he asked it to write an invitation for the party on Saturday at two. The assistant read it back, and Oscar nodded and fell asleep with a paper plane on his chest.

name: word_translator
does: Translates a single word or short phrase into another language, like the word for a hat or how to say you want to paint a wall.
inputs: the word or phrase, and the language you want
people say:
- How do you say hat in Spanish?
- What is the French word for thank you?
- Translate good morning into German.
- I need the Italian for where is the station.
- What do they call a train in Japanese?

Alejandro was in a hurry. His grandmother, who spoke only Italian, would arrive in ten minutes, and he wanted to read her the recipe from the open book on the table. He held up his phone and said, "Say this in Italian, quick: put the plate in the oven for fifty minutes." The assistant said the sentence out loud and wrote it on the screen. Alejandro said, "Zoom in on the words, I can't read them from here." The assistant made the letters bigger. Alejandro read the line twice, set the plate in the oven, and started a timer for fifty minutes. Just then the doorbell rang, and he was ready.

Edward sat in his car outside his house after a long drive. His mother was inside, and she liked fresh air and light in the living room. He typed fast with his thumbs: "open the livng room curtains". The assistant answered, "Opening the living room curtains now." The curtains slid open, and Edward could see his mother wave from the sofa. He typed again: "and the blinds in the kitchen too". The assistant opened those as well. Edward smiled, locked the car, and walked up the path to see her.

Callum worked as a cook, and he got home late in the evening. It was October, and the grass still needed a trim before the rain. He said to his phone, "Start the robot mower at nine tomorrow morning." Then he stopped and said, "No, wait, make it ten. The neighbours sleep in." The assistant changed the start time to ten and said so. Callum also asked it to keep the mower inside the fence at the back, and the assistant saved that rule. A welcome message appeared on his screen: the mower was ready. Callum put his keys down and went to make some soup.

Person: I want to put something on my calendar.
Assistant: Of course. What is the event?
Person: A pancake party. I will slice fruit for it.
Assistant: Sounds nice. What day is the party?
Person: This Saturday afternoon.
Assistant: What time exactly?
Person: Is it true I can pick any time? Say three o'clock.
Assistant: Yes, any time. I added Pancake party on Saturday at three.
Person: Thank you. I am not good with these things.
Assistant: You did very well.

Nora had just moved to a new city, and her phone was almost full. She said, "I need free space on my phone by the end of the week. It is full of guitar videos." The assistant showed her the biggest files and said the videos used eight gigabytes. Nora chose three old videos and asked it to delete them. Then she said, "Where can I buy a charger? I have to go and feed the neighbour's cat." The assistant said there was a phone shop near her building that sold chargers and was open until six. Nora thanked it, grabbed her keys, and walked out.

Budi knelt in his garden under a grey sky when his phone buzzed. He had far too many unread emails. He said, "Show me only half of them, the newest ones first." The assistant read the five newest emails aloud. One said a package would come on Monday. Budi said, "Tell them I'll be home, and put the rest of the mail off until tomorrow." The assistant sent a short reply and hid the old mail until the next day. Budi wiped his hands and went back to push the wheelbarrow of dry leaves to the compost pile.

Person: I want to order a new iron.
Assistant: Sure. Do you want a small one or a large one?
Person: A small one, please. I only have a few shelves left.
Assistant: Where should I send it?
Person: I drive all day, so nobody is home. Send it to my work.
Assistant: What is the address at work?
Person: Fifteen Mill Road.
Assistant: Thank you. Delivery is on Thursday. Shall I finish the order now?
Person: Yes, please.

A bill tells you how much you owe for things like electricity, water or rent. The body of the bill lists what you used and what it costs. Every bill has a due date, which is the last day to pay without a fee. Many people stay calm by setting a reminder a few days early. You can change the date, the amount or the account you pay from. People say, "Remind me before the rent is due," "Pay the water bill on Friday," or "Get me the total for this month." If the total looks too big, you can ask, "Why is it higher than last month?"

Person: whats the water temprature at the beach today
Assistant: Which beach do you mean?
Person: the one near the pier. we have a beach party tonight and i want to swim
Assistant: The water there is about eighteen degrees. Do you want the tide times too?
Person: yes. and remind me to charge my phone before we go
Assistant: Done. I will remind you at five o'clock. Will you bring sun cream?
Person: yes, and my friends bring cooked fish
Assistant: That sounds like a lovely evening.

Errands are small jobs you do outside the house, like going to the post office or the bank. Each place has opening hours, and many have a long line at lunchtime. People often change the day, the time or the thing they need to pick up. They say, "Remind me to collect the parcel," "Move the bank visit to Tuesday," or "What time does the post office close?" Bring an old letter or receipt if you have one, because the clerk may ask for it. Carry heavy parcels with care so your back does not hurt. Hold the door for the next person, and wait your turn.

name: order_printer_ink
does: Orders new ink for your printer with a discount code if you have one, and sends the shop a polite note asking them to hurry the delivery.
inputs: the printer model, which colour is empty, and a discount code if you have one
people say:
- My printer is out of black ink.
- The text is coming out pale, I think it needs new cartridges.
- I need more cyan for my printer, and fast.
- Can you buy ink for my printer before the weekend?
- The red is all gone, get me a new one.

Navigation shows you how to get from one place to another. It uses a map, your position and the traffic to find a route and tell you how long the drive will take. People change the place they are going, the way they travel, or the roads they want to use. They say, "Take me to the airport," "Avoid the motorway," or "Stay off toll roads." On a long trip at night, roads are often quieter, so the drive may be faster. You can also ask, "Find a cafe on the way," if you want a tasty snack. If you miss a turn, the route changes by itself.

On a phone map, a line shows the way to go. Many maps draw the best route in blue and a slower route in grey, and some show heavy traffic in red or purple. People love to check the map before they leave, because it says how long the drive will take. They can change the end point, add a stop, or pick a different road. They say, "Show me another way," "Add a stop at the petrol station," or "Is the road clear?" In a storm with thunder and lightning, drivers often ask for a safer road. The map then looks for roads with less traffic and fewer hills.

When you book a hotel, you choose a city, the nights you will stay, and how many guests. The hotel keeps a room for you until check-in, which is often in the afternoon. People often change the dates, add a guest, or ask for a late check-out. They say, "Make it three nights instead of two," "Add one more guest," or "Can we check out at noon?" Many hotels run a breakfast in the morning, with fruit, bread and carrot juice. If you arrive early, the staff can keep your bags at the front desk, and you can wait outside in the sun or in the lobby.

Meera woke up in a cold room, and her eyes were still blurry. She picked up her phone, but the words looked like tiny ants. "I can't read anything on this thing," she mumbled. The assistant made the text bigger right away. Her screen seemed to freeze for a second, and then large, clear letters appeared. Meera said, "My eyes are too tired for my notes on the board." The assistant understood that she meant the reminder list she kept on her notes board, and it began to read the notes aloud in a calm voice. Meera lay back on the pillow and listened.

A step counter is a small tool inside most phones. It counts your steps while you walk and shows how far you went and how fast you moved. People use it to reach a daily goal, like eight thousand steps. They change the goal, the route or the length of a walk. They say, "Set my goal to ten thousand steps," "How far did I run today?" or "Undo that last walk." If you like a quiet route, you can ask for a path through the park instead of the busy road. Walking a little more each day is good for your body and your mind.

They want to know, with exact spelling and at normal speed, how to say grill in Spanish.
How do you say grill in Spanish?
Spanish for grill?
What is the Spanish word for a grill?
Translate "grill" into Spanish, please.
I run a food stand and there will be two thousand people at the fair, so what is the Spanish word for grill?
Can you tell me how to spell grill in Spanish, the exact word?
How would a person in Madrid say "I will grill the fish"?
Could you please tell me the Spanish word for grill and say it out loud?

Bence was new to the city and wanted to watch a football match. It was a cloudy afternoon, and he sat at the window with a cup of tea. He said, "When does the home team play next?" The assistant said they played on Saturday at seven. Bence asked, "Is that earlier than last week?" The assistant said yes, it was two hours earlier. He then asked it to make a reminder and show him double the usual news about the team, because he wanted to learn more about them. The assistant listed six stories and read the first one aloud. Bence smiled and finished his tea.

An alarm wakes you up at a set time, and a timer counts down from a set length, like ten minutes. People often use alarms for the morning and timers for cooking. When they need a change, they say, "Wake me at six thirty," "Snooze for five minutes," or "Set a timer for the pasta." You can also say, "Cancel my alarm" or "Make it half an hour later." Pay attention to the sound: a soft sound is gentler in the morning. If the sun is bright when you wake up, you might want your sunglasses by the bed. It is good to check the time before you sleep.

Nathan ran a small shop, and he had to take a box of cakes to a customer across town. He carried the box down the stairs and put it in the van. The streets were busy, so he typed on his phone: "fastest way to the bakry on elm street, skip the motorway". The assistant showed a route that took twelve minutes and avoided the motorway. The route followed a thin road along the river. Nathan put the phone on the dashboard, checked the box one more time, and set off.

Amani, a student, was hosting a small party in her flat. Her friends were patient, but the room felt dull. "It's so quiet in here," she said to her speaker. The assistant started a lively playlist at a medium volume. A while later Amani said, "The floor is so sticky." The assistant understood she wanted to remember cleaning, so it added a note: mop the floor after the party. It also reminded her about the payment she owed for the pizza. Amani laughed, paid by phone, and her friends began to dance.

name: close_blinds_by_time
does: Lowers the blinds a set amount at a set time so the red evening sun stays out of your eyes.
inputs: which room, how far to close them (half, most or all), and the time you hope to have them closed
people say:
- The sun is in my eyes.
- Make the bedroom darker at six.
- Close the shades halfway in the kitchen.
- It's too bright in the lounge.
- Can you pull down the blinds before I get home?

name: start_watch_party
does: Starts a show at the same time for you and your friends and sends each friend an invite.
inputs: the show, who to invite, and the time; friends need the streaming app inside their TV, and you can add a reminder to bring the popcorn bucket
people say:
- Let's watch the last episode with Sam tonight.
- Can my sister watch this with me from her house?
- Start the movie for all of us at eight.
- I want to see the game with my cousins, set it up.
- Get everyone to press play together.

A lawn needs a regular cut so the grass stays short and smooth. A robot mower does this by itself: it moves around the garden, cuts a little, and goes back to its charger. In September the grass grows more slowly, so people cut it less often. People change the days, the height of the cut, and where the sprinklers go. They say, "Mow the lawn on Friday," "Cut the grass shorter," or "Move the sprinkler to the back garden." If it rains, they might say, "Skip the mower today." Edges can be trimmed with a small tool.

Joao was in a hurry to catch the bus. The distance to the stop was long, and his flat felt cold. He said, "Set the heating to twenty-two degrees." Then he stopped at the door and said, "No, twenty. It is too expensive to keep it hot while I'm away." The assistant changed the plan to twenty degrees and told him it would warm the flat again at six, when he came home. Joao also asked it to turn off the bathroom heater. He picked up his bag, thanked the assistant, and ran for the bus.

They want the sprinklers to water the garden now.
Water the garden.
Sprinklers on, please.
Give the plants a drink.
The soil is dry, can you start the sprinklers?
I have a late shift at work today, so could you please water the garden for me before I leave?
Please turn on the sprinklers for ten minutes. I have homework to finish and I can't go outside.
The plants look thirsty, so water them.
Run the sprinklers, the water in the old can has gone stale.

name: find_showtimes
does: Finds cinema showtimes for a film and tells you if there are extra late shows.
inputs: the film's name, the town or the cinema near your gym or the old iron bridge, and the day
people say:
- What time is the new Batman film on tonight?
- Is anything good playing near me on Saturday?
- When can I see the dinosaur movie this weekend?
- Are there any late shows after nine?
- I want to take the kids to the cinema tomorrow, what's on?

name: tv_show_alert
does: Tells you when a show you like is about to come on and switches the TV to that channel, so you have time to get a drink if you are thirsty.
inputs: the show's name (like a cooking show about a chocolate factory), the channel, and how many minutes before it starts
people say:
- Tell me when my cooking show starts.
- I always miss the news at six.
- Switch to channel four when the match begins.
- Remind me before the quiz show tonight.
- Don't let me forget the new episode on Friday.

Seren was new to the city, and her science assignment was due on Friday. The library was silent, so she typed on her phone instead of talking: "when is my scienc homework due". The assistant answered, "Friday at nine in the morning." Her project was about how fast, or at what speed, bean plants grow. Seren typed, "how often should i water a bean plant". The assistant said every two days and added a reminder to her calendar. Seren gave a small smile and went back to her notes.

Person: It's freezing in this empty flat.
Assistant: Do you want me to turn on the heating? Which room?
Person: The living room. The movers left the door open and I keep sneezing.
Assistant: I'm sorry. I turned the heating on in the living room. Should it come on daily at this time?
Person: Just today. Can you also pack my boxes?
Assistant: I can't pack boxes, but I can make a list for you.
Person: OK, put a bottle of water on the list.

Zawadi sat on her bed and texted her assistant. Her birthday was close, and she was planning a party. She wrote, "How many days until my birthday, and dim the lights." The assistant said there were forty-one days left and dimmed the lamp. Zawadi wanted a cake in a big size, so she asked for bakery ideas. The assistant listed three bakeries with delicious chocolate cakes and showed the sizes. Zawadi picked the middle size, smiled, and put her phone down beside her pillow.

Sipho got home after a night shift at the hospital and wanted to paint before sleeping. He said, "Open my painting app and select the big blue brush." The assistant opened the app and chose the big blue brush. Sipho was painting a storm with lightning over the sea. Then he said, "Sorry, I mean the thin brush, the lightning needs thin lines." The assistant changed the brush. Sipho also asked for a timer for one hour so he would not forget to sleep, and then he ate a juicy orange while the paint dried.

Fiona was nervous. Her cousin lived in Sydney, and she wanted to call her, but she did not want to wake her. Fiona was lying on her bed after a shower with her hair still wet. She typed just two words: "Sydney time?" The assistant answered, "It is seven in the morning in Sydney." Fiona thought it over, then wrote, "Call Maya." The assistant started the call. Her cousin picked up and said hello, wide awake. Fiona let out a long breath and smiled.

name: bedtime_wind_down
does: Starts a quiet routine before bed that dims the lights, puts the phone on silent and plays soft sounds instead of talk radio.
inputs: your bedtime, the sound you like, and the brand of your sound machine if you have one
people say:
- Help me get ready for bed.
- I want to wind down this evening.
- It's ten o'clock, time to sleep soon.
- Make my room calm before I go to bed.
- I can't sleep, play something soft.

Water comes into a home through a pipe, and a meter counts how much you use. Some of the pipes run inside the wall, so a leak can stay hidden for days. A water heater, often upstairs or in a cupboard, keeps water warm for showers. A leak sensor can warn you when water is on the floor. People ask for changes like, "Turn the water heater down," "Tell me how much water I used this week," or "Warn me if there's a leak." After a long, hot shower, open the window to let the room breathe. Small changes can save water and money.

Person: Tell me what two pounds is in kilos and what 350 Fahrenheit is in Celsius.
Assistant: Two pounds is about 0.9 kilos, and 350 Fahrenheit is about 177 Celsius.
Person: Good. I'm baking for a party in the shop and I'm in a rush.
Assistant: That sounds simple enough. Do you need anything else?
Person: Yes, change my cups of flour to grams.
Assistant: How many cups of flour do you have?
Person: Four.
Assistant: Four cups of flour is about 500 grams.

Javier was a busy parent, and his daughter's school bake sale was on Saturday. He said, "Print the flyer for the bake sale, but don't use colour ink. It costs too much." The assistant printed ten copies in black and white. Javier looked at one and said it was good enough. Then he said, "Email a copy to the bakery on Main Street." The assistant sent the flyer to the bakery and told him the email was gone. Javier pinned a copy on the fridge and went to get dinner ready.

Writing often starts with a rough draft. You put your ideas down first, and then you fix them. Editing means reading it again to spot mistakes in spelling, words and sentences. A word count tells you how long your text is, which matters for homework or emails. People say, "Check my spelling," "Make this shorter," or "How many words is this?" They also say, "Find a better word for big" when the right word will not come. Many people read their text out loud the night before they send it, because mistakes are easier to hear. A calm second look often makes the text better.

Hui came home after a night shift at the hospital. A box of shoes sat by the door. She slid on a shoe and said, "These pinch my toes." The assistant understood she wanted to send them back and asked, "Do you want me to start a return?" Hui said yes. The assistant made a free return label and put a mark on her calendar: drop the box at the post office on Wednesday. She had bought the shoes for a camping trip, so she also asked for a bigger size. The assistant ordered one. Hui yawned and went to bed.

Chen was a child who loved to walk. After school he asked his tablet, "How many steps did I take today, and how far is the park?" The assistant said he had walked six thousand steps, and the park was one kilometre away. Chen said he wanted to go there tonight. His mum began to worry about the dark, so he asked for the walking route to be shown on the map. The assistant showed a lit path. Chen felt proud that he had found a safe way. He put on his shoes and waved to his mum.

Person: I don't want the heater on in my room.
Assistant: Okay. Which room should be warm instead?
Person: The bathroom. I swam for an hour and I'm cold.
Assistant: Do you want it hot or warm?
Person: Warm, not hot. Dad is cutting the grass, so he will come back soon too.
Assistant: I set the bathroom heater to twenty-four degrees and turned the heater in your room off.
Person: Thank you!

They want the room to be warmer.
Warmer, please.
Turn the heat up a bit.
Two degrees more in here.
It's rainy and my desk corner is freezing.
This cold cuts right through me, can you warm it up?
Make it a little warmer, but not as hot as yesterday.
Could you raise the heating by half a degree?
I'm cold, please give me more heat.
Would you please make the study warmer? I will be sitting at my desk all afternoon.

Camille owned a small shop and was planning a party for the neighbourhood. She said, "Add twenty-five people to the guest list." The assistant added them and asked if she wanted invitations sent. Camille said, "I don't know all their emails. Send the invitation to the ones you have." The assistant sent it to nineteen people. She also asked for music and decorations, and the assistant said it could play a happy playlist. Camille was hungry, so she ate a peach while the assistant finished the list.
